answer: Because the glacier solution is checked at the cedar gate and logged, the thread audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 26 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 14 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
